source.title: Faithful Latent Harm Monitors Work No Better Than the Models Own Behaviour at a Matched False Alarm Rate
source.authors: Abhishek Mishra; Sagnik Chatterjee; Suyash Maniyar

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether latent harm reads are distinct from a model’s refusal decision and refines the claim by finding that this depends strongly on read position. It does not perform the original causal ablation or addition.
record.gate_note: The paper tests the distinction between harmfulness judgment and refusal plan, including with Latent Guard’s difference-in-means statistic. It does not ablate or add a direction, perform a weight edit, test jailbreak suppression of the direction, or train against its ablation. Cited findings from other work and values used only for selection or hyperparameter tuning are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Across 15 instruction-tuned models it uses a new cross-model disagreement test and consensus-controlled refusal tests to ask whether harm reads at the instruction token are separate from the refusal decision at the template token. The authors say this corroborates Zhao et al. and extends it across models. It is a different method aimed at V5's question, not the original's causal ablation or addition.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Instruction-token reads are mostly a wording-level judgment, decoupled from the model's refusal once harm and consensus are fixed, and are matched by sentence-embedding classifiers. Template-token reads are the model's refusal plan. Every reader that beats the model's refusal at a matched false-alarm rate is coupled to the decision, effectively a refusal direction, and part of its gain is refusals that string matching misses. So, for the readers tested, faithful latent harm monitors work no better than the model's own behaviour.
record.recipe_differences: The study re-implements Latent Guard’s difference-in-means statistic and examines its association with behavior; it does not use the original single-direction causal ablation or addition intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Read position matters: instruction-token reads are mostly decoupled from refusal, while template-token reads are strongly coupled. At the template token, coupling rises from about 40–50% relative depth and approaches the refusal-probability reference in later layers.

fits_no_version.finding: An Arditi-style harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means projection at the template token tracks each model's own refusal decision. It reaches Π 0.437, about the level of refusal-by-design directions, and catches 0.445 of harmful prompts (Δ +0.079 over string-matched refusal). Latent Guard at that position is indistinguishable from it (paired difference +0.003). At the instruction token the same projection has Π 0.153.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The difference-in-means refusal direction at post-instruction positions is a continuous readout of the model's own refusal propensity, more informative than string-matched refusal labels (correlational, no intervention).

record.problems: Refusal labels rely on string matching and audits find missed refusals and some incorrect labels, especially for OLMoE-1B-7B and Qwen2.5-3B on disagreement items. Harm labels are source-level. The authors test selected readers and positions, not pooled, attention-based, or multi-position probes; they also report one split seed.
record.rows_left_out: Per-model values and additional reader/training-size comparisons are not separately extracted here; the rows record the paper’s aggregate results and position contrasts most directly bearing on V5. The per-model tables and full reader comparison are in Tables 11 and 14.

untested.parts: No causal ablation or addition of a direction and no capability check. Arditi-style projections are used only as passive readers.
No test that jailbreaks suppress the direction and no adversarial training. Wrappers are used only as rewording test items.
No test of affine, cone or multi-direction structure.

No causal test that intervening on the harm read leaves refusal intact, or the reverse. Positions between the instruction and template tokens, and pooled, attention-based or multi-position probes, are not tested. The tests cannot rule out a plan component shared across models.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test; directions are fit per model.
Only the monitor's training data is varied, not how the models' refusal is trained.
Qwen3 is run with thinking disabled, so reasoning models are not tested.

missing.what: Detection under distribution shift at the instruction token, which bears on what the separate harm signal is: Latent Guard pooled AUROC 0.62 vs TF-IDF 0.75; caught 0.23 vs refusal 0.32 (below it in 13 models); linear probe 0.809 vs embedding LR 0.794; persuasion-framing drop 0.10–0.37 in all 15 models.
Stricter control with Jev's harm probability plus consensus: Latent Guard βs at the instruction token falls to 0.11 (above 0 in 3 of 15 models), while at the template token it stays 1.90 (15 of 15).

Reproduction of Zhao et al.'s template-removal labelling on 18 models: removing the template mostly breaks coherence rather than eliciting compliance. For Llama-3-8B the accepted-harmful cell grows from 39 to 226 items while actual compliance falls from 0.88 to 0.10. This questions part of the original evidence for V5.
Unconditioned within-class AUROC at the instruction token: 0.71 on harmful and 0.62 on harmless prompts (above chance in 15 and 12 models), before the consensus control.

Fitting template-token probes to more harm labels moves them off the decision (Π from 0.25 to 0.12) and makes them worse than refusal (Δ from +0.082 to −0.025). No harm component separate from the plan appears at the template token.

record.verdict_notes: The record treated template-token coupling as reversing V5. It is the refusal side of the separation V5 describes, and the authors explicitly corroborate the positional split. The V5 caveats are that the separate harm signal is wording-level and brittle, there is residual instruction-token coupling in strong refusers, and the evidence is correlational. Refusal labels come from string matching, and OLMoE-1B-7B and Qwen2.5-3B are excluded from the cross-model medians. Zhao et al. (2025) is not listed as an original source here, so verdicts on V5 are given.

versions.untested_parts: No causal removal or addition of the direction, and no test of preserved general capabilities.
No test that attacks suppress the direction or that training against ablation adds robustness.
Does not test whether refusal is encoded by an affine structure, cone, or multiple directions.
Tests latent reads at selected positions and their association with refusal, not a complete decomposition of all harmfulness and refusal representations.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test; multiple instruction-tuned models are evaluated, but direction transfer is not tested.
Varies monitor training data, not how or when model refusal behavior is trained.
No test of reasoning models; thinking is disabled for the specified Qwen3 runs.

relation.reason: Its own results bear directly on whether harm and refusal are read separately at the two positions.

tranche.reason: Asks Zhao et al.'s question (harm at tinst vs refusal at tpost) with new methods: cross-model disagreement Π, consensus-controlled βs and within-class AUROC. The authors corroborate V5 and only qualify it (wording-level harm read), so T5 is not the main call.

source_check.notes: All results are correlational, with string-matched behaviour labels; no ablation or steering. Π medians exclude OLMoE-1B-7B and Qwen2.5-3B (78 of 105 pairs). Two things need missing entries: the Appendix A template-removal reproduction (18 models) and the Section 6.1 wording-level evidence behind verdict 3.

statements.correction: Dbeh, LG original recipe: tinst βs 0.14 (TF-IDF 0.09–0.13), Π +0.04 [0.02, 0.06]; tpost βs 1.59, Π +0.23 [0.19, 0.25]. Drew: 19 tinst readers have Π 0.05–0.15; tpost refusal directions have Π 0.44–0.48. Π uses 13 models (OLMoE-1B-7B and Qwen2.5-3B excluded).
statements.problem: None for this study. Π values are medians over 78 pairs of 13 models, not 15.

statements.correction: Figure 3 (Drew, LG original recipe): template-token layers below 40% depth are decoupled; coupling rises from 40–50%. On Dbeh: Π ≤ 0.01 below 30% depth, 0.23–0.26 above 70%.

At fixed consensus: harmless within-class AUROC 0.62, above chance in 6 of 15 models (Llama-3-8B, Gemma-3-27B, OLMo-3-7B, OLMo-3-32B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B, Qwen3-30B-A3B). The harmful side at fixed consensus is 0.59, also above chance in 6. No control: harmless 0.62 in 12 models.
statements.problem: Omits that 0.62 with 6 models above chance is the fixed-consensus value. Without the control it is also 0.62, but above chance in 12 models.

statements.correction: LG as published, pooled AUROC on Drew: median 0.62, below TF-IDF trained on S2000 (0.75) in every model. LG's framing drop is 0.10–0.37 in all 15 models. The S2000 probe removes the framing drop and beats embedding LR on framed prompts by +0.11 (all 15 models). Otherwise the probes tie the sentence-embedding classifiers.
statements.problem: 'The signal fails under persuasion framing' holds for Latent Guard but not for the S2000 linear probe, which removes the framing drop.

statements.correction: Appendix A reproduces Zhao et al.'s labelling with the post-instruction template removed, on 18 models. The refusal drop is explained by coherence loss (drop = −0.836 + 0.826×coherence, R² 0.88). For Llama-3-8B the accepted-harmful cell grows from 39 to 226 items, while its compliance share falls from 0.88 to 0.10. The study therefore labels with the full template.
Limitations: pooled, attention-based and multi-position probes, and positions between b and T, are not tested.

LG as published: pooled AUROC 0.62 vs TF-IDF 0.75; LG has a framing drop in all 15 models. The linear probe beats TF-IDF by +0.060 AUROC (0.809 at S2000), ties the sentence-embedding classifiers, and at S2000 removes the framing drop. Authors' reading: the tinst read is a wording-level judgment, matched by embedding classifiers.
statements.problem: Applies Latent Guard's numbers to 'the decoupled instruction-token harm read' in general. Linear and MLP probes are also decoupled but beat TF-IDF, and the S2000 probe does not fail under framing.
